h1: SiteMind pricing, without the sales fog.
lede: The headline monthly price is only one part of an assistant decision. Compare domains, knowledge limits, credits, setup, and the cost of keeping answers accurate before you subscribe.
body:
Disclosure: this independent guide includes a SiteMind referral link. If you start a paid subscription through it, I may earn a recurring commission at no extra cost to you. This is not a promise of savings or results; verify the provider’s current pricing, privacy, plan, and partner terms before subscribing.

Pricing and plan details checked against SiteMind’s official pricing page on September 9, 2026. Provider terms can change. Use the fit calculator if you want a quick starting point for domains and question volume.

Ready to test the limits? Start a SiteMind trial with my referral link at no extra cost, then compare real question volume against the published plan limits.
Published plan snapshot
PlanPublished priceBest fitKey limits and inclusions
Starter$25/mo
$240/year		One-site pilot1 domain, 200 knowledge units, 1,000 credits/month, website and file ingestion, citations, widget, and a 3-day trial with no card.
Growth$69/mo
$662/year		Small team or multi-site5 domains, 1,500 knowledge units, 5,000 credits/month, analytics, webhooks, and AI actions.
Pro$149/mo
$1,430/year		Higher-volume support10 domains, 6,000 knowledge units, 20,000 credits/month, higher action limits, and broader capacity.

Match the plan to real question volume

Use recent support or sales questions to estimate demand. A credit allowance is not the same thing as a guaranteed number of full conversations, because one conversation can use several answers.

Count every domain and source

List the websites, subdomains, PDFs, documents, and connected knowledge sources you actually need. Confirm the plan covers the source boundary rather than paying for capacity you will not use.

Test the refusal behavior

Ask one question that is clearly documented and one that is not. A useful assistant should ground answers in approved material and make uncertainty visible instead of improvising policy or pricing.

Budget maintenance, not just setup

Set a recurring review for prices, policies, availability, and stale pages. The cheapest plan is not cheap if nobody owns source updates or checks the answers visitors receive.

Confirm the exit path

Before paying, identify the account owner, cancellation controls, data access, source export, renewal date, and what happens to the widget if the subscription ends.

Try it before committing: SiteMind’s public pricing page says the trial starts without a card. If the source, privacy, handoff, and ownership checks above fit your site, start a SiteMind trial with my referral link at no extra cost. Review the official partner information separately from the product decision.
